ENGLISH

Magnetic island topology: coordinates, flux surfaces, and width

Leyan TANG · Reading Notes · I. G. J. Classen (2007), Imaging and Control of Magnetic Islands in Tokamaks, §2.1

A magnetic island is a change in the connectivity of magnetic field lines near a resonant surface. Its familiar island-shaped drawing is a view of magnetic flux surfaces, while the actual field lines continue around the tokamak. These notes connect that picture to three practical questions: Where is a point? Which flux surface is it on? How wide is the island?

1. From nested flux surfaces to an island

In an axisymmetric equilibrium, magnetic field lines lie on nested magnetic flux surfaces. A poloidal cross-section can be drawn as concentric circles in a simplified model; actual tokamak surfaces need not be circular. The field is tangent to these surfaces, so its component normal to an equilibrium surface vanishes. In Classen's circular model, that normal direction is the radial direction.

A resonant radial perturbation can change the topology near one of these surfaces. The result is a helical island flux tube, with its own internal flux surfaces and a separating boundary. Two landmarks appear in the cross-section:

  • O-point: the cross-section of the magnetic axis of the island flux tube; nearby internal contours surround it.
  • X-point: a saddle point of the flux-surface pattern, lying on the separatrix.
  • Separatrix: the boundary between island-interior surfaces and the surrounding surfaces.

The O-point is the island's magnetic axis, rather than the main magnetic axis of the tokamak. Likewise, an X-point in this drawing does not imply that the total three-dimensional magnetic field vanishes there: a large field component along the helical tube remains.

My understanding. Adding a perturbation means adding magnetic-field vectors,

𝐁total=𝐁eq+δ𝐁.\mathbf B_{\mathrm{total}}=\mathbf B_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta\mathbf B.

It does not mean adding two drawings, or moving an intact circle sideways. Flux surfaces are found from the resulting field, and their connectivity can change even when the perturbation is small.

2. Resonance: what the mode numbers mean

The safety factor qq describes the ratio of toroidal to poloidal winding of an equilibrium field line. For the simple circular, large-aspect-ratio model,

q(r)≃rBφR0Bθ.q(r)\simeq\frac{rB_\phi}{R_0B_\theta}.

Here rr is minor radius, R0R_0 is major radius, and BφB_\phi and BθB_\theta are toroidal and poloidal field components. A perturbation with poloidal mode number mm and toroidal mode number nn is resonant where

q(rs)=qs=mn.q(r_s)=q_s=\frac{m}{n}.

Classen defines the helical coordinate and the perturbation phase by

ξ=θ-nmφ,α=mξ-ωt=mθ-nφ-ωt.\xi=\theta-\frac{n}{m}\phi,\qquad \alpha=m\xi-\omega t=m\theta-n\phi-\omega t.

The additional symbol α\alpha is a convenient name for the full phase in these notes; Classen writes this phase as mξ-ωtm\xi-\omega t. The angles θ\theta and φ\phi are poloidal and toroidal angles, and ω\omega is the mode angular frequency. The radial perturbation has the form

Br=Br,0(r)sinα.B_r=B_{r,0}(r)\sin\alpha.

Why is the rational surface resonant? At a fixed time, along an equilibrium field line in this model,

dαdφ=mq-n.\frac{d\alpha}{d\phi}=\frac{m}{q}-n.

At q=m/nq=m/n, the spatial phase is stationary along that line, so the perturbation can act coherently rather than averaging away over successive turns. This explains the geometric resonance condition; it does not by itself determine the growth or saturation of a tearing mode.

For coprime m,nm,n, the island flux tube as a whole closes after mm toroidal turns and nn poloidal turns. Thus a 2/12/1 tube makes two toroidal turns for one poloidal turn. This winding is distinct from the additional motion of an individual field line around the island's own axis.

3. Two coordinates, and a flux-surface label

The signed radial displacement is

y=r-rs.y=r-r_s.
  • y<0y<0: the point is on the smaller-minor-radius side of the resonant surface.
  • y=0y=0: the point has the same minor radius as the resonant surface.
  • y>0y>0: the point is on the larger-minor-radius side.

The pair (y,ξ)(y,\xi) describes a position in the local helical cross-section. The coordinate ξ\xi is angular; yy is a radial distance. Neither coordinate alone specifies which island flux surface passes through a point.

For an isolated island in the local constant-shear, constant-ψ\psi approximation, with the positive magnetic shear used in this chapter, Classen's Eq. 2-3 can be rearranged as

Ω=8y2w2-cosα.\Omega=\frac{8y^2}{w^2}-\cos\alpha.

Equivalently, both radial branches of a contour are

y=±w22Ω+cosα.y=\pm\frac{w}{2\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{\Omega+\cos\alpha}.

The square root is real only where Ω+cosα≥0\Omega+\cos\alpha\ge0. The symbol ww denotes the full island width. At a fixed phase of the rotating island, Ω\Omega labels the perturbed magnetic flux surfaces:

Value of Ω\OmegaInterpretation
Ω=-1\Omega=-1O-point
-1<Ω<1-1<\Omega<1Surfaces inside the island
Ω=1\Omega=1Separatrix, including the X-point
Ω>1\Omega>1Surfaces outside the island

↔ Scroll sideways to view all columns

In this model, Ω<-1\Omega<-1 is not accessible. A constant-Ω\Omega contour represents a cut through a flux surface. The value Ω\Omega is a label of the surface, rather than a length measured from the O-point.

4. Reading question ①: is y measured from the O-point or the X-point?

Question. If y=0y=0, must the point be the O-point, the X-point, or a point on a particular Ω\Omega surface?

Resolved. The reference for yy is the equilibrium resonant radius rsr_s. To identify the point and its flux surface, the helical phase is also needed. Setting y=0y=0 gives

Ω=-cosα.\Omega=-\cos\alpha.

At t=0t=0, an O-point has α=0\alpha=0 modulo 2π2\pi and Ω=-1\Omega=-1; an X-point has α=π\alpha=\pi modulo 2π2\pi and Ω=1\Omega=1. Other phases on the same y=0y=0 line give intermediate values of Ω\Omega. So the same radial coordinate can pass through the O-point, an interior surface, or the X-point.

The words “inner” and “outer” need care: the sign of yy distinguishes the smaller- and larger-radius sides of the resonant surface. It does not distinguish the inside and outside of the island. For example, at y=w/4y=w/4,

Ω(α=0)=-12,Ω(α=π)=32.\Omega(\alpha=0)=-\frac{1}{2},\qquad \Omega(\alpha=\pi)=\frac{3}{2}.

These two points have the same positive yy, but the first is inside the island and the second is outside. The test for island membership is Ω\Omega, which depends on both radial position and phase.

5. Reading question ②: why is w the full width?

Question. Why does the island width include both sides of the O-point rather than just the distance from the O-point to the separatrix?

Resolved. Width measures the greatest radial span of the separatrix. At the phase through the O-point, α=0\alpha=0, the separatrix satisfies Ω=1\Omega=1, so

y=±w2.y=\pm\frac{w}{2}.

Its two radial boundaries are therefore at rs-w/2r_s-w/2 and rs+w/2r_s+w/2. Their separation is

w=(rs+w2)-(rs-w2).w=\left(r_s+\frac{w}{2}\right)-\left(r_s-\frac{w}{2}\right).

The distance from the O-point to either boundary on this radial cut is the half-width, w/2w/2. These equal half-widths follow from the symmetric local approximation; a more general island need not be symmetric about the original resonant radius.

At other phases, the local radial span is smaller. On the separatrix,

y=±w2|cos(α/2)|.y=\pm\frac{w}{2}|\cos(\alpha/2)|.

Thus its local radial span is w|cos(α/2)|w|\cos(\alpha/2)|: it reaches ww through the O-point and shrinks to zero at an X-point. The full width is the maximum span, not the span of every radial cut.

6. A contour plot is not a drawing of complete field lines

The island-shaped curves show magnetic flux surfaces in the helical cross-section. The dominant magnetic-field component points along the helical flux tube, out of this plane. The weaker in-plane components produce the slow radial and angular motion seen after following a field line over many toroidal turns.

The equilibrium field's in-plane component, denoted B*B^* by Classen, is locally proportional to yy and changes sign across the resonant surface. At y=0y=0, this component vanishes; the total equilibrium field does not. Combined with the radial perturbation, it gives the familiar island pattern.

My understanding. A field line can tilt only slightly from the equilibrium direction at each point, yet accumulate a substantial radial excursion over a long distance. The change in topology is a statement about connectivity, rather than a claim that the whole magnetic field has rotated by a large angle.

7. Two winding numbers describe two different motions

The island tube's global winding qs=m/nq_s=m/n describes its path around the tokamak. Classen introduces a second winding number for field lines inside that tube:

qtm=mtmntm.q_{\mathrm{tm}}=\frac{m_{\mathrm{tm}}}{n_{\mathrm{tm}}}.

It counts toroidal turns per turn around the island's own magnetic axis. In the turn-counting description, a line makes ntmn_{\mathrm{tm}} turns around the O-point while making mtmm_{\mathrm{tm}} turns around the torus. This description does not require every field line to close after a finite integer number of turns; the winding can be interpreted as an asymptotic ratio.

Approaching the separatrix from inside,

qtm→∞.q_{\mathrm{tm}}\to\infty.

The local circulation around the island axis becomes increasingly slow near the X-point, so more toroidal travel is required for one such circulation. This limit is not a divergence of the ordinary equilibrium safety factor qsq_s.

8. Perturbed flux amplitude and island width

Classen uses the perturbed poloidal flux function ψ\psi, with units of Tm2\mathrm{T}\,\mathrm{m}^2, defined by

𝐁~=∇φ×∇ψ,ψ=ψ0cosα.\widetilde{\mathbf B}=\nabla\phi\times\nabla\psi,\qquad \psi=\psi_0\cos\alpha.

Here ∇φ\nabla\phi is the gradient of the toroidal angle, rather than an electric-potential gradient. The tilde denotes the perturbed poloidal field. In the constant-ψ\psi approximation, ψ0\psi_0 changes negligibly across the narrow island region; this does not make the full phase-dependent ψ\psi spatially constant.

Using R≃R0R\simeq R_0 and evaluating equilibrium quantities at rsr_s, Eqs. 2-4 and 2-7 give

Br,0=mψ0rsR0,w=4rsqsBr,0mBθ|q's|,q's=dqdr|rs.B_{r,0}=\frac{m\psi_0}{r_sR_0},\qquad w=4\sqrt{\frac{r_sq_sB_{r,0}}{mB_\theta|q'_s|}},\qquad q'_s=\left.\frac{dq}{dr}\right|_{r_s}.

With the positive-shear and positive-amplitude conventions used here, Eq. 2-8 becomes

ψ0=Cw2,C=BθR0q's16qs=rsBφq's16qs2.\psi_0=Cw^2,\qquad C=\frac{B_\theta R_0q'_s}{16q_s}=\frac{r_sB_\phi q'_s}{16q_s^2}.

The second expression for CC uses the circular, large-aspect-ratio expression for qq. Consequently,

w=ψ0C.w=\sqrt{\frac{\psi_0}{C}}.

What the relation tells me. The width depends on the perturbation amplitude and the equilibrium magnetic shear and field. At fixed equilibrium parameters, quadrupling ψ0\psi_0 doubles ww. If the equilibrium changes, CC must also be reconsidered. This local formula is not applicable at zero magnetic shear, where its assumptions fail.

The units provide a useful check: CC has units of tesla, so Cw2Cw^2 has units of Tm2\mathrm{T}\,\mathrm{m}^2. Some literature uses a flux function with units of Tm\mathrm{T}\,\mathrm{m} instead; its normalization must be converted before comparing numerical formulas.

9. Review checkpoints

  1. What distinguishes a magnetic island from a shifted circular equilibrium surface?
  2. Which turns are counted by mm and nn, and why is q=m/nq=m/n resonant?
  3. Why can two points with the same positive yy lie on opposite sides of the separatrix?
  4. What additional information is needed when a point has y=0y=0?
  5. Where are Ω=-1\Omega=-1 and Ω=1\Omega=1, and what does a constant-Ω\Omega curve represent?
  6. Where is the radial span equal to ww, and why is the O-point-to-boundary distance only w/2w/2?
  7. Why does qtmq_{\mathrm{tm}} diverge near the separatrix while qsq_s remains finite?
  8. If CC stays fixed and ψ0\psi_0 becomes four times larger, what happens to ww?

10. Reference

I. G. J. Classen. Imaging and Control of Magnetic Islands in Tokamaks. PhD thesis, Eindhoven University of Technology, 2007. §2.1, printed pages 12–14, Eqs. 2-1–2-8 and Fig. 2-2. University record · DOI: 10.6100/IR627226.

中文

磁岛拓扑：坐标、磁通面与宽度

Leyan TANG · Reading Notes · I. G. J. Classen（2007），Imaging and Control of Magnetic Islands in Tokamaks，第 2.1 节

磁岛是共振面附近磁力线连通方式的改变。常见的“岛形”图展示的是磁通面，而真实磁力线仍沿托卡马克绕行。这份笔记把这幅图像与三个实际问题联系起来：一个点在哪里？它属于哪个磁通面？磁岛到底有多宽？

1. 从嵌套磁通面到磁岛

在轴对称平衡中，磁力线位于一层层嵌套的磁通面上。简化模型可以把极向截面画成同心圆，但真实托卡马克的磁通面不一定是圆。磁场与磁通面相切，因此沿平衡磁通面法向的分量为零。在 Classen 采用的圆形模型里，这个法向就是径向。

共振的径向扰动可以改变其中一个磁通面附近的拓扑，形成具有内部磁通面和分隔边界的螺旋磁岛通量管。在截面上，有几个关键标志：

  • O 点：磁岛通量管自身磁轴的截面；附近的内部等值线围绕它。
  • X 点：磁通面图样中的鞍点，位于分离面上。
  • 分离面（separatrix）：磁岛内部磁通面与周围磁通面之间的边界。

O 点代表的是磁岛自己的磁轴，而不是托卡马克的主磁轴。同样，截面上出现 X 点，也不意味着该处的三维总磁场为零：沿螺旋通量管方向仍有很强的磁场分量。

我的理解。 叠加扰动，是叠加磁场矢量：

𝐁total=𝐁eq+δ𝐁.\mathbf B_{\mathrm{total}}=\mathbf B_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta\mathbf B.

这不等于把两幅图相加，也不是把一个完整的圆横向挪动。磁通面由叠加后的磁场决定；即使扰动很小，磁力线的连通方式也可能改变。

2. 共振：模数到底在数什么

安全因子 qq 描述平衡磁力线的环向绕行与极向绕行之比。在圆形、大纵横比的简化模型中，

q(r)≃rBφR0Bθ.q(r)\simeq\frac{rB_\phi}{R_0B_\theta}.

其中 rr 是小半径，R0R_0 是大半径，BφB_\phi 和 BθB_\theta 分别是环向和极向磁场分量。极向模数为 mm、环向模数为 nn 的扰动，在满足下式的位置共振：

q(rs)=qs=mn.q(r_s)=q_s=\frac{m}{n}.

Classen 定义的螺旋坐标，以及扰动的完整相位为

ξ=θ-nmφ,α=mξ-ωt=mθ-nφ-ωt.\xi=\theta-\frac{n}{m}\phi,\qquad \alpha=m\xi-\omega t=m\theta-n\phi-\omega t.

这里额外引入 α\alpha，只是为了简写完整相位；Classen 原文使用的是 mξ-ωtm\xi-\omega t。θ\theta、φ\phi 分别是极向角和环向角，ω\omega 是模的角频率。径向磁场扰动写为

Br=Br,0(r)sinα.B_r=B_{r,0}(r)\sin\alpha.

为什么有理面会共振？在固定时刻，沿这个模型中的一条平衡磁力线，

dαdφ=mq-n.\frac{d\alpha}{d\phi}=\frac{m}{q}-n.

在 q=m/nq=m/n 处，空间相位沿这条线保持不变，因此扰动可以连续、相干地作用，而不是在反复绕行中相互抵消。这解释了几何上的共振条件，但仅凭这一条件，还不能决定撕裂模怎样增长或饱和。

若 m,nm,n 互质，整个磁岛通量管在环向绕行 mm 圈、极向绕行 nn 圈之后闭合。例如，2/12/1 通量管在环向绕两圈、极向绕一圈。这种绕行要与一条磁力线围绕磁岛自身磁轴的额外运动区分开。

3. 两个坐标与一个磁通面标签

有正负号的径向位移是

y=r-rs.y=r-r_s.
  • y<0y<0：位于共振面的小半径一侧。
  • y=0y=0：小半径与共振面相同。
  • y>0y>0：位于共振面的大半径一侧。

(y,ξ)(y,\xi) 描述局部螺旋截面中的一个位置。ξ\xi 是角坐标，yy 是径向距离。只知道其中一个坐标，都不足以判断这个点所在的磁岛磁通面。

对于局部磁剪切近似为常量、采用 constant-ψ\psi 近似的孤立磁岛，并使用本章的正磁剪切约定，Classen 的式 2-3 可以改写为

Ω=8y2w2-cosα.\Omega=\frac{8y^2}{w^2}-\cos\alpha.

等价地，一条等值线的上下两个径向分支为

y=±w22Ω+cosα.y=\pm\frac{w}{2\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{\Omega+\cos\alpha}.

只有在 Ω+cosα≥0\Omega+\cos\alpha\ge0 时，根号才有实数值。ww 表示磁岛全宽。在旋转磁岛的某一固定相位，Ω\Omega 为扰动后的磁通面编号：

Ω\Omega 的取值含义
Ω=-1\Omega=-1O 点
-1<Ω<1-1<\Omega<1磁岛内部的磁通面
Ω=1\Omega=1分离面，包括 X 点
Ω>1\Omega>1磁岛外部的磁通面

↔ 横向滑动查看完整表格

这个模型中不存在 Ω<-1\Omega<-1 的位置。恒定 Ω\Omega 的等值线代表磁通面的一个截面；Ω\Omega 是磁通面标签，而不是从 O 点量起的一段长度。

4. 阅读疑问①：y 是从 O 点还是 X 点量起的？

疑问。 当 y=0y=0 时，这个点一定是 O 点、X 点，或者某个指定 Ω\Omega 磁通面上的点吗？

已解决。 yy 的参照是平衡共振面半径 rsr_s。要确定具体位置及其磁通面，还需要螺旋相位。令 y=0y=0，得到

Ω=-cosα.\Omega=-\cos\alpha.

在 t=0t=0 时，O 点满足 α=0\alpha=0 模 2π2\pi，因此 Ω=-1\Omega=-1；X 点满足 α=π\alpha=\pi 模 2π2\pi，因此 Ω=1\Omega=1。同一条 y=0y=0 线上的其他相位，对应中间的 Ω\Omega 值。因此，同一个径向坐标可以经过 O 点、内部磁通面或者 X 点。

“内”和“外”的说法需要明确参照：yy 的正负区分的是共振面的小半径一侧和大半径一侧，不能用来区分磁岛内部与外部。例如，在 y=w/4y=w/4 处，

Ω(α=0)=-12,Ω(α=π)=32.\Omega(\alpha=0)=-\frac{1}{2},\qquad \Omega(\alpha=\pi)=\frac{3}{2}.

这两个点有相同的正 yy，但前者在磁岛内部，后者在磁岛外部。判断是否在岛内，要看同时依赖径向位置和相位的 Ω\Omega。

5. 阅读疑问②：为什么 w 是全宽？

疑问。 为什么磁岛宽度包含 O 点两侧，而不是仅指从 O 点到分离面的距离？

已解决。 宽度衡量的是分离面在径向上的最大跨度。在经过 O 点的相位 α=0\alpha=0 处，分离面满足 Ω=1\Omega=1，于是

y=±w2.y=\pm\frac{w}{2}.

两个径向边界分别位于 rs-w/2r_s-w/2 和 rs+w/2r_s+w/2，二者的距离为

w=(rs+w2)-(rs-w2).w=\left(r_s+\frac{w}{2}\right)-\left(r_s-\frac{w}{2}\right).

在这条径向截线上，从 O 点到任一边界的距离都是半宽 w/2w/2。两侧半宽相等，是这个对称局部近似的结果；更一般的磁岛不一定关于原共振半径对称。

其他相位处的径向跨度更小。对于分离面，

y=±w2|cos(α/2)|.y=\pm\frac{w}{2}|\cos(\alpha/2)|.

因此，局部径向跨度为 w|cos(α/2)|w|\cos(\alpha/2)|：经过 O 点时达到 ww，在 X 点处缩小到零。全宽是最大跨度，而不是每条径向截线上的跨度。

6. 等值线图并不是完整磁力线的轨迹图

岛形曲线展示的是螺旋截面中的磁通面。主要磁场分量沿螺旋通量管方向，指向这个平面之外；较弱的面内分量，则决定沿磁力线走过很多个环向周期后才显现出来的缓慢径向与角向运动。

Classen 用 B*B^* 表示平衡磁场在这个平面内的分量。它在局部与 yy 成正比，并在共振面两侧改变符号。在 y=0y=0 处，这个面内分量为零，但总平衡磁场并不为零。它与径向扰动结合，形成熟悉的磁岛图样。

我的理解。 磁力线在每个位置相对平衡方向的偏转可以很小，但沿线走过很长距离后，仍会累积出显著的径向跨度。拓扑的改变讲的是连通关系，并不意味着整个磁场方向发生了很大的转动。

7. 两种绕行，两个绕行数

磁岛通量管整体的 qs=m/nq_s=m/n 描述它怎样绕行托卡马克。对于通量管内部的磁力线，Classen 另外引入

qtm=mtmntm.q_{\mathrm{tm}}=\frac{m_{\mathrm{tm}}}{n_{\mathrm{tm}}}.

它表示围绕磁岛自身磁轴转一圈所需的环向绕行圈数。按圈数描述，就是磁力线环向绕行 mtmm_{\mathrm{tm}} 圈时，围绕 O 点转过 ntmn_{\mathrm{tm}} 圈。这并不要求每条磁力线都在有限整数圈数后闭合；绕行数也可以理解为长期绕行圈数的比值。

从磁岛内部趋近分离面时，

qtm→∞.q_{\mathrm{tm}}\to\infty.

在 X 点附近，围绕磁岛磁轴的局部环流越来越慢，因此完成一次环流需要走过越来越多的环向圈数。这不是普通平衡安全因子 qsq_s 发散。

8. 扰动磁通幅值与磁岛宽度

Classen 使用扰动极向磁通函数 ψ\psi，其单位为 Tm2\mathrm{T}\,\mathrm{m}^2，定义为

𝐁~=∇φ×∇ψ,ψ=ψ0cosα.\widetilde{\mathbf B}=\nabla\phi\times\nabla\psi,\qquad \psi=\psi_0\cos\alpha.

这里的 ∇φ\nabla\phi 是环向角的梯度，并不是电势的梯度。波浪号表示扰动极向磁场。在 constant-ψ\psi 近似中，ψ0\psi_0 在狭窄磁岛区域内的变化可以忽略；这不等于随相位变化的完整 ψ\psi 在空间中处处相同。

取 R≃R0R\simeq R_0，并在 rsr_s 处计算平衡量，式 2-4 和式 2-7 给出

Br,0=mψ0rsR0,w=4rsqsBr,0mBθ|q's|,q's=dqdr|rs.B_{r,0}=\frac{m\psi_0}{r_sR_0},\qquad w=4\sqrt{\frac{r_sq_sB_{r,0}}{mB_\theta|q'_s|}},\qquad q'_s=\left.\frac{dq}{dr}\right|_{r_s}.

按这里采用的正磁剪切和正幅值约定，式 2-8 写为

ψ0=Cw2,C=BθR0q's16qs=rsBφq's16qs2.\psi_0=Cw^2,\qquad C=\frac{B_\theta R_0q'_s}{16q_s}=\frac{r_sB_\phi q'_s}{16q_s^2}.

CC 的第二种写法使用了圆形、大纵横比近似下的 qq 表达式。因此，

w=ψ0C.w=\sqrt{\frac{\psi_0}{C}}.

这条关系给我的认识。 宽度既依赖扰动幅值，也依赖平衡磁剪切和磁场。在平衡参数固定时，ψ0\psi_0 增大到四倍，ww 增大到两倍。平衡发生变化时，CC 也需要重新计算。这个局部公式不能直接用于零磁剪切处，因为此时推导假设已经失效。

单位可以帮助检查：CC 的单位为特斯拉，所以 Cw2Cw^2 的单位是 Tm2\mathrm{T}\,\mathrm{m}^2。部分文献使用单位为 Tm\mathrm{T}\,\mathrm{m} 的磁通函数；比较数值公式前，需要先统一归一化约定。

9. 复习检查

  1. 磁岛与一个被横向移动的圆形平衡磁通面有什么区别？
  2. mm 和 nn 分别计数哪种绕行，为什么 q=m/nq=m/n 处会共振？
  3. 为什么具有相同正 yy 的两个点，可能分别在分离面内外？
  4. 当一个点满足 y=0y=0 时，还需要什么信息才能确定它的位置？
  5. Ω=-1\Omega=-1 和 Ω=1\Omega=1 分别在哪里，恒定 Ω\Omega 的曲线代表什么？
  6. 哪个位置的径向跨度等于 ww，为什么从 O 点到边界只有 w/2w/2？
  7. 为什么分离面附近 qtmq_{\mathrm{tm}} 发散，而 qsq_s 仍有限？
  8. 如果 CC 固定，ψ0\psi_0 增大到四倍，ww 会怎样变化？
